_NOTE: Partial capture. Public state captured via Playwright browser_evaluate against the live SWE on staging during a real login flow. Doken capture deferred to the runtime warm-up (must be obtained mid-SWE-login; OIDC access_token is in-memory only on the Account Console after redirect; private localStorage bytes are intentionally not captured per the SWE error-reporting allowlist). Schema: see load-harness/src/runSign.ts for UserFixture / RealmFixture / OrkInfo interfaces and SERIALIZATION-NOTES.md for the wire-format design.

realm._vvkid_NOTE: Extracted from the SWE URL query string `gVVK=...`. This IS the vvkid for tide-metrics-load realm — stable across all users in the realm. Round-5 correction: there is NO server-side fetch path for this — the Keycloak admin /realms/{r}/keys endpoint is unauth-404 and the public JWKS does not list the tide-vendor-key. The warm-up SEEDS this value (from fixture/env) and Path α in oidc.ts patches it in place from the first user's SWE URL.
realm._vvkPublic_NOTE: Same as vvkid in this realm — gVVK on the URL is the vendor's public vault key, and tide-js's Point class accepts it via fromHex. Two distinct fields preserve room to diverge later (e.g. if a future tide-js Point.Serialize() uses base64).
realm._voucherURL_NOTE: The host part + path + clientId are stable; sessionId + tabId are per-login. Captured value during the test login: sessionId=utpldoi2GOTSu-lnyfbFpa7g, tabId=-cYh3E6JYNs. runSign() bakes the per-session sessionId+tabId at iteration time. Path α (oidc.ts) overwrites this with the live pattern from the first SWE URL — so a stale clientId in this sample doesn't sink the warm-up.
realm._orks_NOTE: Placeholder shape only — DO NOT bake live ORK identities here. The warm-up fetches this once per run from <homeOrkUrl>/Network/Authentication/Node/Some, which returns a BARE JSON array of objects with lowercase camelCase fields {id, index, publicKey, paymentPublicKey, url}. The harness maps id→orkID, url→orkURL, publicKey→orkPublic, paymentPublicKey→orkPaymentPublic. `index` (cohort position) is unused by v1. Cohort size is staging-dependent — observed 5 on 2026-06-02 (down from 10 at the original capture). 0 orks from a 200 response is treated as a fatal bootstrap error.
realm._signedSettings_NOTE: Captured from the SWE URL `signedSettings=...&settingsSignature=...`. Stable across all logins for the realm. The harness doesn't validate the signature — that's TideCloak's job — but it does need to know RegOn=true means registration is signed-on. Stored under realm because it is realm-scoped, not user-scoped.
realm._swe_url_NOTE: These are the params TideCloak's TideIdentityProvider.performLogin redirect URL carries. All present per Phase-1 idp-extensions PM audit. authorizerPack is hex-encoded; the others are base64. These REALM-level values are stable across logins. v1 captures `gVVK` and `voucherURL` via Path α (oidc.ts); the others are reference-only for now.

users._vuid_NOTE: The Tide-derived hash that TideCloak's first-broker-login screen populated as the auto-username. It's the SHA-256 of the user's CMK-derived identity (per the tide-IdP-extensions setup).
users._doken_NOTE: OIDC access_token issued by TideCloak after the SWE CMK-auth completes. Captured by the warm-up via the harness /warmup/oidc/begin + /callback + /warmup/oidc/await flow (standard PKCE; no prototype hacking). v1: ~5min Keycloak default lifetime — re-warm before each load run is the operational path. v1.1: use refreshToken below to mint a fresh access_token before runSign().
users._refreshToken_NOTE: Optional v1 field — captured alongside doken by the warm-up. SENSITIVE: longer lifetime than access_token; treat as a secret in handling. v1: harness does not consume it; v1.1 may use it for refresh-on-demand if first-run latency forces us off rewarm-before-each-run. Server.ts /warmup/oidc/await/:state is the only egress point.
users._dokenExpiresAt_NOTE: Optional v1 field — ISO timestamp computed by the warm-up as capturedAt + expires_in (seconds) from the token endpoint. Used in v1.1 to decide when to refresh.
